h.strategy: Before writing hypotheses, decide which field values typically appear in strong configurations and which in weak ones. A condition that fixes such a value mostly selects strong (or weak) parents. Use this deliberately. Strong parents have little room left, so edits that usually help gain less there, and edits that usually hurt lose more. Weak parents sit near a floor, so harmful edits cost little and helpful edits gain a lot. Write at least six hypotheses where this quality effect predicts the opposite direction to the most obvious story about how the parts connect. Write the remaining ones on the strongest effects you are confident in. Use only conditions that many parents satisfy. Spread hypotheses across edited fields and edit values. In each 'why', name the quality mechanism.

hyps.why: A parent with edge 0 removed is weak and far from the ceiling, so adding a strong conv on the output edge gains much more than in a cell that is already strong.
A parent with a strong conv on edge 5 is already near the ceiling, so the usually helpful skip shortcut has little room left to add.
Strong parents sit high and have more accuracy to lose, so deleting the direct edge costs more there than in weak parents near the floor, even though the conv path offers redundancy.
When edge 5 is none the parent is weak and near the floor, so a harmful downgrade to pooling costs little.
The parent is a weak, near-floor cell where edge 2 is already starved of input, so removing it costs almost nothing compared with strong parents.
A parent with a strong conv on the direct edge is already high quality, leaving little headroom for an additional conv 1x1 to help.
Strong parents with conv on edge 0 are close to saturation, so extra capacity on edge 1 gives diminishing gains compared with weak parents.
A weak parent with edge 5 removed is near the floor, so also cutting edge 0 costs little compared with cutting it from a strong cell.
Without the direct edge the parent is weak with much room to improve, so a strong conv on edge 4 yields a larger gain.
A parent with edge 1 removed is weak and low-capacity, so adding the strong conv on the first edge gains more than in an already well-connected strong parent.
